title: A Comparative Analysis of Pickup Forecasting Methods for Customer Arrivals in Airport Carparks
authors: Andreas Papayiannis; Paul Johnson; Peter Duck
summary: 28 pickup variants on 15 months of pre-booking data from four UK airport car parks at 7-56 day horizons.
key_findings: Additive beat multiplicative; advanced slightly beat classical; Add-Advan-HW best at 7 days (MAE 24.42 for CP1).
coster_takeaway: Directly reusable recipe for forecasting outbound pallets from shipment notices on hand.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
authors: Isaac Gibbs, Emmanuel Candès
summary: Online adjustment of the miscoverage level around any forecaster.
key_findings: Achieves the target long-run coverage under arbitrary distribution shift. Robust on two real datasets with clear shifts.
coster_takeaway: Wrap every rung's 48 h interval with ACI per class. It keeps coverage honest after layout and WMS-rule changes. Cap the width to avoid infinite sets.

title: An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload to the master surgical schedule
authors: P. T. Vanberkel, R. J. Boucherie, E. W. Hans, J. L. Hurink, W. A. M. van Lent, W. H. van Harten
venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society 62(10), 1851-1860
summary: Analytical model that maps the master surgical schedule to distributions of ward occupancy, admissions and discharges.
key_findings: Schedule-driven inflows plus stay distributions give exact occupancy distributions. Used to redesign the schedule at the Netherlands Cancer Institute.
coster_takeaway: Production plans play the role of the surgical schedule. An analytic convolution of planned inflows with dwell distributions is a fast, explainable alternative or check for the Monte Carlo simulator.

title: Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics
authors: Hayo Bos, Stef Baas, Richard J. Boucherie, Erwin W. Hans, Gréanne Leeftink
summary: Combines doctors' expected discharge dates with data-driven length-of-stay distributions via Poisson-binomial and convolution models to give full bed-census distributions.
key_findings: Integrating expert discharge estimates with empirical LoS distributions gave precise census distributions on real hospital data.
coster_takeaway: Direct template for rung 2. Each occupied cell is a 'patient' with a planned exit (ship date, WO consumption) plus an empirical deviation. Convolve per class to get P(fill > 80% / 90%).

title: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting
authors: Ansari, Shchur, Küken, Auer, Han, Mercado, Rangapuram, Shen, Stella, Zhang, Goswami, Kapoor, Maddix, Guerron, Hu, Yin, Erickson, Desai, Wang, Rangwala, Karypis, Wang, Bohlke-Schneider
summary: A pretrained model that handles univariate, multivariate and covariate-informed forecasting zero-shot through group attention over related series and covariates. It supports past-only, known-future and categorical covariates and outputs 21 quantiles.
key_findings: State of the art on fev-bench, GIFT-Eval and Chronos Benchmark II. On fev-bench: win rate 90.7%, skill 47.3%, median runtime 3.6 s. Covariate tasks are won 'by a wide margin'. About 300 series/s on an A10G GPU.
coster_takeaway: Use as the rung-4 candidate. Feed the 5 classes as one group, plans and calendar as known-future covariates, and defrag or floor-buffer counts as past-only covariates. Calibrate its quantiles with CQR/ACI before alerting.

title: Evaluating probabilistic classifiers: Reliability diagrams and score decompositions revisited (CORP)
authors: Timo Dimitriadis, Tilmann Gneiting, Alexander I. Jordan
summary: Stable reliability diagrams based on PAV isotonic regression, plus a CORP Brier-score decomposition.
key_findings: Consistent, optimally binned and reproducible reliability diagrams, with a miscalibration measure that extends to any proper scoring rule.
coster_takeaway: Check the calibration of the 'P(class >= 90% within 48 h)' alert with CORP diagrams and a Brier decomposition. With few events, report resampling bands.

title: fev-bench: A Realistic Benchmark for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Shchur, Ansari, Turkmen, Stella, Erickson, Guerron, Bohlke-Schneider, Wang
summary: 100 forecasting tasks in 7 domains, 46 with covariates (30 known dynamic, 24 past dynamic, 19 static). Results are aggregated as bootstrapped win rates and skill scores, with the fev library for reproducible evaluation.
key_findings: Probabilistic (SQL) win rates: Chronos-2 91.4%, TiRex 83.3%, TimesFM-2.5 79.6%, FlowState 73.3%, Toto 72.4%, TabPFN-TS 69.7%, Moirai-2.0 67.4%, Chronos-Bolt 67.0%, TFT 51.4%, Stat. Ensemble 45.5%, CatBoost 34.4% (point 52.4%), Seasonal Naive 19.6%. The authors write that 'existing TSFMs often miss accuracy by ignoring covariates'.
coster_takeaway: Pick covariate-aware foundation models (Chronos-2, TabPFN-TS, TimesFM-3, Timestral, TiRex-2) because Coster's value lies in the plans. Reuse fev's win-rate and skill-score scheme for the model ladder.

title: Forecasting with Chronos-2 (AutoGluon tutorial)
authors: AutoGluon team
summary: How to run Chronos-2 with known and past covariates, LoRA or full fine-tuning, and ensembles in AutoGluon.
key_findings: Electricity load: MASE 0.696 with covariates vs 1.278 for univariate Bolt-small. Fine-tuning gave 0.688 (266 s vs 0.5 s). Air temperature alone cut error by about 32%. More covariates do not always help.
coster_takeaway: Copy this workflow: known_covariates_names set to planned inflow/outflow per class plus calendar, then inspect covariate importance and drop plan features that do not help.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.), Ch. 10 Dynamic regression models
authors: Rob J. Hyndman, George Athanasopoulos
summary: Regression with ARIMA errors. Future predictor values are required, and lagged predictors are possible.
key_findings: Prediction intervals do not account for uncertainty in the predictors, so they are conditional on the assumed plan.
coster_takeaway: Fit the change in fill on planned net flow with ARIMA errors as the statistical rung 2. Add plan-slip uncertainty separately (Monte Carlo or conformal), because ARIMAX bands assume the plan is exact.

title: From Tables to Time: Extending TabPFN-v2 to Time Series Forecasting (TabPFN-TS)
authors: Hoo, Müller, Salinas, Hutter
summary: Recasts forecasting as tabular regression on calendar and seasonal features plus known-future covariates, solved zero-shot by TabPFN.
key_findings: Ranked 1st on GIFT-Eval in Jan 2025 (repo). Supports known-future covariates, drops past-dynamic and static covariates. Defaults moved to TabPFN-3.5 in Sep 2026.
coster_takeaway: Strong fit for a tiny dataset with known plans: frame each class-day as a row with planned net flow features. Prefer LOCAL mode so data stays on premises, and switch off telemetry.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2501.02945 (Hoo, Mueller, Salinas, Hutter, Jan 2025) and the repo confirm TabPFN-TS, the Jan 2025 GIFT-Eval #1 claim, known-future-only covariates (past dynamic and static dropped) and the Sep 2026 v1.3.0 switch to TabPFN-3.5.

title: Harmonizing Operations Management of Key Stakeholders in Wafer Fab Using Discrete Event Simulation
authors: Georg Seidel; Ching Foong Lee; Ai Mei Kam; Boon Ping Gan; Chew Wye Chan; Andre Naumann; Patrick Preuss
venue: Proceedings of the 2017 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Automatic nightly 7-day simulation forecast from the current fab state (lots, equipment, blockings, wafer-start plan) for WIP per work centre.
key_findings: Aggregated accuracy >90% within three months; gap metric for validation; users compare last 3 days simulated vs actual.
coster_takeaway: Run the rung 2 simulator nightly, validate with a gap metric, show recent forecast-vs-actual for trust.

title: How to determine slot sizes in a unit-load warehouse
authors: Luis F. Cardona (and co-author(s))
summary: Slot profile design: choose slot heights and quantities so that a service level is met, defined as the probability that all pallets present in a period can be stored.
key_findings: Multiple slot heights save 29-45% space; 2 slot types already ~26.7% on average; Gaussian approximation of aggregate inventory by height class.
coster_takeaway: Adopt its service-level definition for Coster's 'pallets that find no compatible free cell' KPI and its Gaussian aggregate-inventory model as a quick probabilistic baseline per class.

title: Impact of required storage space on storage policy performance in a unit-load warehouse
authors: Xiaolong Guo; Yugang Yu; Rene B.M. de Koster
summary: Models required storage space (RSS) as a function of space sharing between items in a class and compares random, full-turnover and class-based policies.
key_findings: RSS exceeds average inventory and grows as fewer items share a class; full turnover-based storage needs ~50% more space than random; <=5 classes optimal.
coster_takeaway: Directly explains why splitting cells into 5 rigid classes (and reserving wide cells) loses effective capacity; quantify the 'space-sharing loss' of Coster's classes in the simulator.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. IJPR 54(8):2405-2418 (2016) PDF states RSS exceeds average inventory, full turnover-based storage needs nearly 50% more space than random, and optimum is no more than five classes.

title: Leakage in Data Mining: Formulation, Detection, and Avoidance
authors: Shachar Kaufman, Saharon Rosset, Claudia Perlich
summary: Formalises leakage as illegitimate information about the target. Proposes tagging every observation with legitimacy (timestamps) and a learn-predict separation.
key_findings: 'No-time-machine' rule: features must predate the target. Databases that keep a single timestamp per record make separation hard. Real competition examples are given.
coster_takeaway: Store every plan and log row with an as-of timestamp, and build backtest features only from rows recorded before the origin. Use this to justify asking Coster for daily plan exports.

title: Monte-Carlo Simulation Based on Patient-Individual Distributions for Supporting Intensive Care Occupancy Management
authors: Arne Witteborg; Rainer Borgstedt; Markus Gunther; Gerrit Jansen; Michael Romer
summary: ML-produced, expert-validated patient LOS distributions plus planned admissions/discharges feed a Monte Carlo of daily ICU occupancy.
key_findings: Counterfactual on 2019 data: simple policy would have avoided critical occupancy in about 70% of cases and smoothed occupancy.
coster_takeaway: Per-pallet exit distributions + plan -> Monte Carlo -> probability of critical fill; allow planner overrides.

title: Real-time forecasting of COVID-19 bed occupancy in wards and Intensive Care Units
authors: Stef Baas; Sander Dijkstra; Aleida Braaksma; Plom van Rooij; Fieke J. Snijders; Lars Tiemessen; Richard J. Boucherie
summary: Network of two time-varying infinite-server queues (ward, ICU) with Kaplan-Meier LOS and transfer probabilities; 1,000 Monte Carlo runs give point forecasts, intervals and maximum occupancy.
key_findings: ICU 95% PI coverage 74-97%; ward coverage lower due to unmodelled parameter uncertainty; 3-day maximum-occupancy forecasts most useful; adopted in hospital dashboards.
coster_takeaway: Blueprint for rung 2: KM dwell curves + flow inputs + Monte Carlo; add parameter uncertainty to avoid under-coverage.

title: Short term hospital occupancy prediction
authors: Steven Littig, Mark Isken
summary: Short-term hospital census prediction for decision support (keywords: occupancy, census prediction, patient flow).
key_findings: Abstract and methods were not available on the opened page. The paper is cited as a foundational short-term occupancy prediction study.
coster_takeaway: Background reference for patient-flow-based short-term census prediction. Read the full text only if building the analytic rung.

title: When Do Foundation Models Pay Off? A Break-Even Analysis of Pretrained Time Series Forecasters
authors: Nicholas Tan Jerome, Frank Simon
summary: Break-even analysis on 30 datasets comparing zero-shot and LoRA-fine-tuned Chronos, Moirai and Lag-Llama against Naive, ETS, ARIMA and XGBoost at 2-100% of the training data.
key_findings: Foundation models won on 15 of 30 datasets at every training fraction. Classical methods won on 6 even at 2% of the data. On the other 9, break-even was between 24 and 8,361 samples. Rule: with fewer than 700 samples and non-negligible seasonality, use zero-shot and skip fine-tuning. LoRA fine-tuning can degrade short series. Covariates and horizon are not analysed.
coster_takeaway: With about 70 daily points per class, use foundation models zero-shot and do not fine-tune. Still run a classical and an XGBoost baseline, because on some datasets classical methods win even with little data.

title: A comparison of forecasting methods for hotel revenue management
authors: Larry R. Weatherford; Sheryl E. Kimes
venue: International Journal of Forecasting (per citation; not on fetched PDF)
summary: Compares pickup, regression, smoothing and other methods on Choice and Marriott hotel arrivals.
key_findings: Exponential smoothing and pickup most robust; pickup minimised MAPE; combining recommended.
coster_takeaway: Use pickup on shipment-notice curves for outbound beyond the notice horizon.

title: A method for developing and validating simulation models for automated storage and retrieval system digital twins
authors: Andrea Ferrari, Antonio Carlin, Carlo Rafele, Giovanni Zenezini
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: UML conceptual model and AnyLogic DES of an AS/RS including the WMS/WCS logic (tasks to missions), validated with a 72-run design of experiments.
key_findings: The deterministic model underestimated storage time. Stochastic timings brought the median error to 0.49%. The coded priority-based assignment matched real location choices in all trials.
coster_takeaway: Coding Coster's real allocation cascade (including the wide-cell hold-back) matters more than physics. Validate the simulator by replaying known days and checking class choices against the movement log.

title: A Multi-Stage Discrete Event Simulation Approach for Scheduling of Maintenance Activities in a Semiconductor Manufacturing Line
authors: Wolfgang Scholl; Marcin Mosinski; Boon Ping Gan; Peter Lendermann; Patrick Preuss; Daniel Noack
venue: Proceedings of the 2012 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Short-term online model from current state gives 7-day arrival forecasts per work centre to pick maintenance days; traffic-light readiness.
key_findings: Maintenance on forecast low-arrival days was followed by WIP decreases instead of increases.
coster_takeaway: Use the forecast to time disruptive activities (e.g., consolidation, defrag, maintenance) on low-occupancy days.

title: A Queuing Approach to Parking: Modeling, Verification, and Prediction
authors: Hamidreza Tavafoghi; Kameshwar Poolla; Pravin Varaiya
summary: Time-varying arrival and duration queue validated on 29 truck parking sites over 16 months; micro/macro real-time probabilistic predictors.
key_findings: Forecasting reduces to parameter estimation; lower bound on prediction error derived.
coster_takeaway: Micro per-pallet residual-duration forecasting with an error lower bound for benchmarking.

title: A simple and explainable model for park-and-ride car park occupancy prediction
authors: Andreas Kaltenbrunner; Josep Ferrer; David Moreno; Vicenc Gomez
summary: Occupancy = arrivals - departures with truncated-normal profiles; TNL adds a capacity limit to estimate fill time and unserved cars.
key_findings: Test errors mostly below 4%; capacity-limited model >10x better where car parks fill.
coster_takeaway: Include an explicit overflow term per class (pallets to floor buffer).

title: A survey of literature on automated storage and retrieval systems
authors: Kees Jan Roodbergen; Iris F.A. Vis
summary: Reviews 30 years of AS/RS research in production and distribution: configuration, travel time, storage assignment, dwell point, sequencing.
key_findings: Most models are static; calls for dynamic, self-adaptive storage assignment and integration with other material handling systems (conveyors, vehicles).
coster_takeaway: Use its taxonomy (random / closest-open-location / class-based) to describe WLog's policy; closest-open-location fills racks near I/O first, relevant to aisle/class occupancy patterns.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. EJOR 194(2):343-362 PDF confirms 30-year AS/RS review, call for dynamic/self-adaptive assignment and integration with other handling systems, and closest-open-location filling near I/O.

title: ACN-Data: Analysis and Applications of an Open EV Charging Dataset
authors: Zachary J. Lee, Tongxin Li, Steven H. Low
venue: e-Energy '19 (ACM International Conference on Future Energy Systems)
summary: Introduces an open dataset of EV charging sessions at Caltech and JPL workplace garages, including user-entered requested departure times and energy.
key_findings: User-entered departure estimates were the least reliable predictor: departure SMAPE 25.8% (Caltech) and 18.6% (JPL) vs 15.9% and 12.3% for per-user Gaussian mixture models.
coster_takeaway: Declared plans can be beaten by learned corrections. Test 'plan as covariate + learned slip' vs 'plan as truth' for Coster's shipment and production timing.

title: Aggregating Predicted Individual Hospital Length of Stay to Predict Bed Occupancy for Hospitals
authors: Mattis Hartwig; Simon Schiff; Sebastian Wolfrum; Ralf Moller
summary: Aggregates individual LOS predictions into hospital occupancy forecasts on MIMIC-IV and simulates error patterns.
key_findings: Symmetric LOS errors matter more for occupancy accuracy than total error size.
coster_takeaway: When predicting pallet exits, avoid biased (one-sided) errors; calibrate on aggregate occupancy, not just per-pallet MAE.

title: An Easy Approach to Extending a Short Term Simulation Model for Long Term Forecast in Semiconductor Industry
authors: Marcin Mosinski; Tobias Weissgaerber; Soo Leen Low; Boon Ping Gan; Patrick Preuss
venue: Proceedings of the 2017 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Short-term (35-day) model generated daily from live databases extended to long-term forecasts.
key_findings: Short-term accuracy >90%; long-term quality >90% for three weeks then degraded; flow compression cut runtime 104 -> 45 min.
coster_takeaway: Expect accuracy to fall after ~3 weeks; simplify non-critical steps as delays.

title: AutoGluon-TimeSeries: AutoML for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
authors: Shchur, Turkmen, Erickson, Shen, Shirkov, Hu, Wang
summary: AutoML library that ensembles statistical and ML models for point and quantile forecasts in a few lines of code.
key_findings: Beat a range of methods on 29 datasets and often the best-in-hindsight combination.
coster_takeaway: Use as the harness for rung 4 (Chronos-2 plus tabular plus statistical ensemble) with known_covariates_names set to the plan columns.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2308.05566 (comment: AutoML Conference 2023; PMLR 224) confirms authors, 29 datasets and frequent improvement over best-in-hindsight combination.

title: Backward Simulation: A Customer-Focused Diversification of Fab Simulation Applications in a Highly Automated Semiconductor Production Line
authors: Wolfgang Scholl; Patrick Preuss; Christoph Laroque; Madlene Leissau
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Infineon Dresden 7-day lot-arrival/WIP forecast from live data (30+ sources) with green/yellow/red display; backward simulation for due dates.
key_findings: SimBack raised on-time completions from 21/50 to 47/50 lots; data-quality checks needed.
coster_takeaway: Traffic-light presentation of class saturation per day; build validation checks into the data pipeline.

title: Bursty Arrivals, Smooth Sojourns: Non-Poissonian Temporal Dynamics in a Logistics Warehouse
authors: Alfonso de Miguel-Arribas, Yamir Moreno
summary: Analyses one month of event data from a large Spanish 3PL warehouse: inter-arrival, shelving and departure times and outbound-buffer sojourns. Code and derived public tables are on GitHub.
key_findings: Arrivals and departures are bursty with little memory (B about 0.78-0.85). Sojourns are smooth and log-normal; about 70% end within 24 h. The buffer behaves as a non-stationary renewal system with a weekly cycle (weekend build-up, Monday/Tuesday clearing).
coster_takeaway: Do not assume Poisson inflows in the simulator. Use calendar-aware, flow-specific stay-length distributions, and include weekday/end-of-week features in the residual model.

title: Capacity Forecasting in a Backup Storage Environment
authors: Mark Chamness
summary: Piecewise linear regression with validation rules forecasts time-to-full for over 10,000 backup systems and sends proactive alerts.
key_findings: Median R2 0.93; forecasts withheld for 40-50% of systems daily; false positives often from human actions.
coster_takeaway: Let the alert engine abstain when inputs are invalid and express alerts as time-to-full.

title: Conformal PID Control for Time Series Prediction
authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Emmanuel J. Candès, Ryan J. Tibshirani
summary: Treats interval width as a PID controller: quantile tracking, an error integrator and a scorecaster.
key_findings: Deterministic long-run coverage without infinite sets. Generalises ACI. Tighter sets than ACI near nominal 90% on electricity demand.
coster_takeaway: A drop-in, more stable alternative to ACI for the alert bands. The scorecaster can learn month-end widening.

title: Conformal Prediction Algorithms for Time Series Forecasting: Methods and Benchmarking
authors: Andro Sabashvili
summary: Reviews conformal approaches for time series (relaxed exchangeability, panel-as-unit, residual-dynamics models, online learning) and benchmarks them with AutoARIMA on monthly sales.
key_findings: Multi-step split conformal met the 90% coverage threshold with the best efficiency (Winkler score).
coster_takeaway: Start with simple per-horizon split conformal and add ACI or PID only if backtest coverage drifts.

title: Conformal prediction interval for dynamic time-series (EnbPI)
authors: Chen Xu, Yao Xie
summary: Distribution-free sequential intervals built from bootstrap-ensemble residuals, without data splitting.
key_findings: Approximately valid finite-sample marginal coverage for strongly mixing errors.
coster_takeaway: Use via MAPIE TimeSeriesRegressor(method='enbpi', cv=BlockBootstrap) around the rung-3 model, with one model per horizon.

title: Conformal Time-series Forecasting
authors: Kamile Stankeviciute, Ahmed M. Alaa, Mihaela van der Schaar
summary: Extends inductive conformal prediction to multi-horizon forecasts from any predictor.
key_findings: Guaranteed multi-horizon coverage under minimal exchangeability assumptions. Implemented in MLForecast and sktime (with an optional Bonferroni correction across horizons).
coster_takeaway: Basis for per-horizon conformal bands (h = 1..14). Use the Bonferroni variant if all 14 days must be covered jointly.

title: Conformalized Quantile Regression
authors: Yaniv Romano, Evan Patterson, Emmanuel J. Candès
summary: Calibrates quantile-regression bands with conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample coverage with adaptive widths.
key_findings: Proven coverage. Usually shorter intervals than other conformal approaches.
coster_takeaway: Use to recalibrate Chronos-2 or LightGBM quantiles before computing P(fill >= 90%).

title: Darts documentation: forecasting model and covariate support table
authors: Unit8 / Darts contributors
summary: Per-model matrix of univariate/multivariate, probabilistic, past, future and static covariate and multi-series support, including foundation and conformal models.
key_findings: Chronos2Model supports past and future covariates. TimesFM2p5Model and TiRexModel have no covariates in Darts. Regression models (LightGBM, CatBoost, XGBoost, linear) support all covariate types.
coster_takeaway: Check each candidate's covariate support here before building it into the backtest. Plans must be passed as future_covariates.

title: Data-Driven Bed Capacity Planning Using Mt/Gt/inf Queueing Models with an Application to Neonatal Intensive Care Units
authors: Maryam Akbari-Moghaddam; Douglas G. Down; Na Li; Catherine Eastwood; Ayman Abou Mehrem; Alexandra Howlett
summary: Time-varying arrivals and empirically fitted LOS in an M_t/G_t/inf model for NICU capacity scenarios in Calgary.
key_findings: Daily occupancy often exceeds 100% even when long-run targets are met; static 85% rule performs poorly; LOS variability matters.
coster_takeaway: Base 80/90% alerts on daily exceedance probabilities, not averages.

title: Does Data Vintage Matter for Forecasting?
authors: Dean Croushore, Tom Stark
venue: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Working Paper 99-15
summary: Builds a real-time data set of quarterly vintages and compares forecasts made with real-time and with latest-available data.
key_findings: Real-time and final-data forecasts can differ substantially for some variables. Judging methods only on the latest vintage can mislead comparisons.
coster_takeaway: Treat Coster's plans like revisable macro data. Backtests on final plans overstate simulator accuracy, so evaluate on stored plan vintages once daily exports exist.

title: Duration-of-Stay Storage Assignment under Uncertainty
authors: Michael Lingzhi Li, Elliott Wolf, Daniel Wintz
summary: Predicts pallet duration of stay in cold-storage warehouses from arrival date, product group, customer type, weight, locations and product description, using 8.44 M pallets from 37 facilities.
key_findings: ParallelNet reached 29% MAPE vs 41% for the best baseline. Product group, arrival date and customer type matter most. Live deployment reduced labour by up to 21%.
coster_takeaway: Estimate a dwell-time distribution per material or LU type from LU first-seen and last-seen dates in the snapshots. Use it for outflows of LUs with no planned exit (purchased components, QC, empties).

title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
authors: Hertel, Nikoltchovska, Pütz, Mikut, Schäfer, Hagenmeyer
summary: Zero-shot Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS with weather and calendar covariates for TSO day-ahead load, compared with a Transformer trained on years of data. Adds SHAP via temporal and covariate masking.
key_findings: Both foundation models were competitive zero-shot, and their explanations matched domain knowledge.
coster_takeaway: Compute covariate-masking SHAP for Chronos-2 to show planners that the forecast responds to planned inflows. This builds trust in a black-box rung 4.

title: Forecast Evaluation for Data Scientists: Common Pitfalls and Best Practices
authors: Hansika Hewamalage, Klaus Ackermann, Christoph Bergmeir
venue: arXiv:2203.10716 (preprint for Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery)
summary: Practitioner guide to evaluating forecasts: leakage, rolling-origin (tsCV) evaluation, error measures and benchmarks.
key_findings: Defines leakage as using data not available at inference time. Rolling-origin schemes are especially prone to it, as is preprocessing over the full series before splitting.
coster_takeaway: Fit scalers, encoders and residual models only on data before each backtest origin. Use sliding-window rolling origins and compare every rung against persistence.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
authors: Arkadiusz Lipiecki, Rafał Weron
summary: Nine zero-shot variants from five foundation-model families vs EPF benchmarks in DE, PL and ES (2021-2025), for accuracy and trading value.
key_findings: Only TabPFN models consistently and significantly beat the benchmarks. Statistical gains did not translate fully into profit.
coster_takeaway: Include TabPFN-TS in the rung-4 shortlist. Judge models on the alert decision (cost of missed vs false alerts), not only CRPS.

title: Hotel booking demand datasets
authors: Nuno Antonio, Ana de Almeida, Luis Nunes
summary: Two hotel booking datasets (40,060 resort and 79,330 city bookings, 31 variables) extracted from PMS databases, covering arrivals from July 2015 to August 2017, including cancellations.
key_findings: Each booking has lead time, stay length (weekday/weekend nights), cancellation flag and reservation status date. Bookings were checked against the change log as of the day before arrival.
coster_takeaway: Build an 'on-the-books vs realised occupancy' backtest here first. It is the cleanest public stand-in for planned arrivals + stay length + plan slips.

title: Initialization of Online Simulation Models
authors: Andre Hanisch; Juri Tolujew; Thomas Schulze
venue: Proceedings of the 2005 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Compares model generation from data with parent-model synchronisation and child forecast runs; case of density warnings in a station concourse.
key_findings: Synchronisation gives better initialisation; unmeasured state must be assumed; corrections against measured totals are model-specific.
coster_takeaway: Keep a synchronised state model and correct it against measured class totals each morning.

title: Lead time forecasting for supplier management using machine learning
authors: Fredrik Sitje, Felix Waldschock
venue: Master's thesis, Chalmers University of Technology (case at Maxon)
summary: Predicts actual supplier lead times from ERP purchase-order lines (11,565 lines after filtering) with CatBoost and other models.
key_findings: CatBoost reached 0.804 binned accuracy vs 0.343 for supplier estimates. Engineered process features were essential, and heavy filtering and domain knowledge were needed.
coster_takeaway: Build Monte Carlo slip distributions for purchased inflows from PO promised dates vs actual receipts, per supplier. Do not trust PO dates or confirmations as-is.

title: lifelines: survival analysis in Python
authors: Cameron Davidson-Pilon
summary: Pure-Python survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Nelson-Aalen, regression); MIT licence.
key_findings: Light dependencies (NumPy, SciPy, pandas).
coster_takeaway: First choice for KM dwell curves per material/load-unit group.

title: M5 accuracy competition: Results, findings, and conclusions
authors: Makridakis, Spiliotis, Assimakopoulos
summary: Results of forecasting 42,840 hierarchical Walmart unit-sales series.
key_findings: All top methods were pure ML. 4 of the top 5 used LightGBM. All top-50 used cross-learning. All winners used external information (prices, events): ARIMAX was about 13% better than ARIMA and ESX about 6% better than ES. The winner averaged 6 models and was 22.4% better than the best benchmark.
coster_takeaway: Supports rung 3: a global LightGBM across classes with plan features. Exogenous information is where the gains come from. Ensembles help.

title: Master surgery scheduling with consideration of multiple downstream units
authors: Andreas Fugener; Elias W. Hans; Rainer Kolisch; Nikky Kortbeek; Peter T. Vanberkel
summary: Exact demand distribution on ICU and wards for a given block schedule plus exact and heuristic optimisation of downstream costs.
key_findings: Downstream resources can be included in schedule design.
coster_takeaway: Multiple downstream units = multiple cell classes; compute and optimise jointly.

title: Maximizing space utilization in unit-load warehouses
authors: Luis Cardona Olarte
venue: University of Louisville (Electronic Theses and Dissertations)
summary: Dissertation on unequal slot heights and space utilisation in unit-load storage.
key_findings: Reviews Lee et al. (1999, 2005) and develops slot-profile and layout models.
coster_takeaway: Open-access source for the slot-profile math to reuse in the per-class capacity model.

title: Minimizing Bed Occupancy Variance by Scheduling Patients under Uncertainty
authors: Anne van den Broek d'Obrenan; Ad Ridder; Dennis Roubos; Leen Stougie
summary: Expected ward occupancy = existing patients + scheduled patients x P(LOS > t - surgery day); ILP levels occupancy with Monte Carlo feasibility check.
key_findings: 526 patients in 139 blocks solved in ~290 s; ignoring levelling scheduled more patients but raised ward variability to 49-64%.
coster_takeaway: Exactly the rung 2 formula; also a template for later plan-levelling what-if.

title: Modeling COVID-19 hospital admissions and occupancy in the Netherlands
authors: Rene Bekker; Michiel uit het Broek; Ger Koole
summary: Admissions forecast with an LP method; occupancy predicted by fitting residual lengths of stay and applying queueing theory; used for national patient distribution.
key_findings: Improved accuracy and trust in forecasts; supported short- and long-term decisions.
coster_takeaway: Model residual dwell of current stock separately from new inflows.

title: Mt/G/inf queues with sinusoidal arrival rates
authors: Stephen G. Eick; William A. Massey; Ward Whitt
summary: Formulas for the time-varying mean number of busy servers in an M_t/G/inf queue; with suitable initial conditions the count is Poisson.
key_findings: Peak congestion lags peak arrivals; congestion varies over a narrower range than offered load; mean is a linear operator on the arrival rate.
coster_takeaway: Use arrivals convolved with dwell survival as a closed-form occupancy model; expect occupancy peaks to lag inbound peaks.

title: Optimal design of rack structure with modular cell in AS/RS
authors: Young Hae Lee; Moon Hwan Lee; Sun Hur
summary: Proposes AS/RS racks with modular cells instead of equally sized cells, with the modular cell size as a decision variable, so loads of different sizes can be stored with higher space utilisation.
key_findings: Equal-size cells waste space with mixed load heights; modular cells increase utilisation and flexibility when demand mix fluctuates.
coster_takeaway: Academic basis for Coster's 5 cell classes; zone-based unequal cells (Coster's design) are inflexible when the mix shifts, so forecast the mix per class.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. ScienceDirect abstract (IJPE 98(2):172-178, 2005) proposes modular cells with cell size as decision variable; it does not mention an MINLP minimising lost space or building on Lee et al. (1999).

title: Optimal Storage Capacity under Random Storage Assignment and Class-based Assignment Storage Policies
authors: Moon-Kyu Lee
venue: Journal of the Korean Institute of Industrial Engineers 25(2)
summary: Analytic models for optimal AS/RS storage capacity under random and class-based policies with a service-level constraint.
key_findings: Capacity chosen to balance space cost and space shortage while meeting a desired service level.
coster_takeaway: Supports framing alerts as P(class demand > class capacity) and the 80/90% thresholds as service-level choices.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. KoreaScience record: Moon-Kyu Lee, J. Korean Inst. Industrial Engineers 25(2):274-281 (1999); analytic RAN and class-based capacity models minimising space and shortage cost under a service-level constraint.

title: Optimization of transporting time through load shuffling in automated storage and retrieval system and evaluation via demonstration experiments
authors: Hiroki Ishikura; Makoto Tsukamoto; Shingo Egi; et al.
venue: Japan Journal of Industrial and Applied Mathematics
summary: 0-1 IP load shuffling in a factory AS/RS (ROHTO) during non-production hours using next-day retrieval jobs; tested in simulator and real plant.
key_findings: Up to ~72% less crane time for next-day retrievals in simulation; much smaller gain in the real plant because next-day information was incomplete.
coster_takeaway: Shows value of plan information quality: Coster's frozen assembly week and hourly production timing are assets; log plan versions to measure this effect.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Springer page (JJIAM 42(5), 2025) confirms 0-1 IP load shuffling at ROHTO factories, ~72% simulated reduction for retrieval targets, smaller real-plant gain due to limited next-day info; article is open access.

title: Optimization of warehouse storage capacity under a dedicated storage policy
authors: M.-K. Lee; Elsayed A. Elsayed
summary: Space shortage occurs when demand exceeds capacity; extra need met by leased space; nonlinear model minimises owned plus leased space cost.
key_findings: Optimal owned capacity can be found iteratively; overflow space is an explicit decision variable.
coster_takeaway: Coster's ~800-slot floor buffer plays the role of leased overflow space; model overflow volume explicitly as an output, not a failure.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. T&F abstract (IJPR 43(9):1785-1805, 2005) matches: dedicated full-turnover storage, shortage met by leased space, nonlinear model minimising owned plus leased cost, iterative optimal search.

title: Proactive production activity control by online simulation
authors: Olivier Cardin; Pierre Castagna
venue: International Journal of Simulation and Process Modelling 6(3)
summary: DES used as a short-term forecasting tool for production activity control, starting each run from the current real state.
key_findings: Feasibility shown on a real-size flexible manufacturing system.
coster_takeaway: Start every forecast run from the 06:00 snapshot rather than warming up.

title: Re-warehousing vs. healing: Strategies for warehouse storage location assignment
authors: Monika Kofler; Andreas Beham; Stefan Wagner; Michael Affenzeller; Werner Achleitner
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Logistics and Industrial Informatics (LINDI)
summary: Compares full re-warehousing with daily small cleanup tasks (healing).
key_findings: A few healing moves per day reach assignments competitive with full re-warehousing over months.
coster_takeaway: Supports Coster's continuous defrag over the 3-4-monthly manual consolidation; forecast should include the steady defrag flow.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. LINDI 2011 abstract (pp. 77-82) states a small number of daily cleanup (healing) tasks reach a good assignment over months, competitive with re-warehousing.

title: ruptures: change point detection in Python (Truong, Oudre, Vayatis 2020 review)
authors: Charles Truong, Laurent Oudre, Nicolas Vayatis
summary: Offline change-point detection library (Pelt, Binseg, BottomUp, Window, Dynp, KernelCPD) with many cost functions.
key_findings: BSD-2. Includes evaluation metrics and synthetic signals.
coster_takeaway: Run PELT on class fill and flow series to date the August layout break and any later WMS-rule change, and train only on the comparable segment.

title: scikit-survival: A Library for Time-to-Event Analysis Built on Top of scikit-learn
authors: Sebastian Polsterl
summary: Python survival analysis library with penalized Cox, Random Survival Forest, Survival SVM and censored-data metrics (GPL-3).
key_findings: scikit-learn compatible API.
coster_takeaway: Use for dwell-time models once enough completed stays exist; note GPL-3.

title: scoringrules: weighted scoring rules documentation
authors: scoringrules developers
summary: Python implementations of CRPS, twCRPS, owCRPS and vrCRPS for ensembles, plus energy and variogram scores.
key_findings: twCRPS equals the CRPS after censoring at threshold t. Multiplying scores by weights is improper (forecaster's dilemma).
coster_takeaway: Use scoringrules.twcrps_ensemble on sample paths with t = 0.8 for model comparison.

title: Shared Storage Policies Based on the Duration Stay of Unit Loads
authors: Marc Goetschalckx; H. Donald Ratliff
summary: Duration-of-stay based shared storage policies for unit-load warehouses; optimal policy for balanced input/output and heuristics otherwise.
key_findings: DoS-based classes reduce travel time versus dedicated, random and turnover-based storage.
coster_takeaway: Background for using dwell-time classes in allocation/defrag later.

title: Simulation-based Optimization of Sequencing Buffer Allocation in Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems for Automobile Production
authors: Christian Urnauer; Eva Bosch; Joachim Metternich
summary: Several production buffers share one AS/RS with limited capacity; simulation-based greedy heuristic distributes capacity among buffers.
key_findings: Marginal benefit of buffer positions saturates; convex solution space; shared AS/RS capacity allocation matters.
coster_takeaway: Analog of allocating AW cells among departments/classes; use marginal-value logic to evaluate WLog's reservation of wide cells.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. WSC 2019 paper confirms shared AS/RS capacity among sequencing buffers, greedy simulation-based heuristic, saturation of additional buffer positions and (empirically) convex solution space.

title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
authors: Tilmann Gneiting, Adrian E. Raftery
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 102(477)
summary: Theory of proper scoring rules, including CRPS, quantile and interval scores.
key_findings: CRPS generalises absolute error. The interval score rewards both coverage and narrowness.
coster_takeaway: Score Coster's bands with CRPS, pinball loss and the interval score. Score alert probabilities with the Brier score.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. DTIC report of the Gneiting-Raftery paper (JASA 102(477), 2007) covers proper scoring rules, CRPS generalising absolute error, and the interval score accounting for width and coverage.

title: Temporal Fusion Transformers for Interpretable Multi-horizon Time Series Forecasting
authors: Lim, Arik, Loeff, Pfister
summary: Attention architecture built around static, past-observed and known-future inputs, with quantile outputs and variable selection.
key_findings: Interpretable multi-horizon forecasts. In fev-bench it now trails pretrained models (51.4% vs 91.4% probabilistic win rate).
coster_takeaway: A conceptual template (static, past and known-future inputs) for Coster's feature design. Too data-hungry to train now.

title: The physics of the Mt/G/inf queue
authors: S. G. Eick; W. A. Massey; W. Whitt
summary: Structural results for M_t/G/inf: the time-dependent mean depends on the full service-time distribution, not only its mean.
key_findings: Stationary-excess distribution of service time is key; effect of service variability reverses between rising and falling arrival rates.
coster_takeaway: Fit full dwell-time distributions, not just mean dwell, when arrivals vary (e.g., month-end).

title: The warehouse reshuffling problem with swap moves and time limit
authors: Jan-Niklas Buckow; Sigrid Knust
venue: EURO Journal on Transportation and Logistics
summary: High-bay AS/RS with twin-shuttle crane; reshuffling at night or in breaks with limited time; random storage during operations.
key_findings: Only a subset of pallets can be reshuffled in the time window; heuristics and simulated annealing; industrial setting.
coster_takeaway: Mirrors Coster's defrag (idle-time, limited missions/week); cap defrag capacity in the simulator by available idle crane time.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. ScienceDirect page (EURO J. Transp. Logist., 2023) confirms twin-shuttle AS/RS reshuffling with a time limit, simulated annealing and heuristics on instances based on a real company setting.

title: Time-dependent analysis for refused admissions in clinical wards
authors: R. Bekker; A. M. de Bruin
summary: M_t/H/s/s model with infinite-server approximations to quantify how time-varying admissions affect bed needs and refusals.
key_findings: Week-weekend pattern drives refusals far more than daily pattern; higher LOS variability stabilises bed requirement; day-of-week bed requirement method.
coster_takeaway: Treat floor-buffer overflow as 'refused admissions' and quantify day-of-week risk.

title: TimesFM-3: a zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting (Google Research blog)
authors: Google Research
summary: 330M-parameter model pretrained on over 1 trillion points. Natively multivariate, with past and past-future (known) covariates and 9 quantiles. Available on GitHub, Hugging Face and BigQuery AI.FORECAST.
key_findings: Reported as the top pretrained model on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME for point and probabilistic metrics. Self-hosted 3.0 weights are non-commercial (GitHub license note).
coster_takeaway: Strong candidate technically, but production use at Coster would need BigQuery ML or TimesFM 2.5 (Apache-2.0). Use 3.0 only for offline comparison unless the license is cleared.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models (announcement)
authors: Mistral AI
summary: Four sizes (5M-209M) of multivariate probabilistic models with past-only, known-future and categorical covariates, 21 quantiles, 32k context and CPU inference.
key_findings: Vendor-reported 1st among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench (209M). The 28M model reportedly beats Chronos-2 on GIFT-Eval and TIME. Modified MIT weights.
coster_takeaway: Add as a watch-list challenger to Chronos-2. It can run on a plant PC without a GPU. Wait for independent leaderboard confirmation.

title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
authors: Podest, Pichler, Bürger, Zólyomi, Voggenberger, Berghammer, Klotz, Böck, Klambauer, Hochreiter
summary: Extends TiRex to multivariate forecasting with past and future-known covariates and constant-cost streaming.
key_findings: Reports top zero-shot results on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench. 38.4M active params (+44.1M for multivariate).
coster_takeaway: A small, covariate-aware challenger to Chronos-2. Check license and package availability before adding it to the backtest.

title: Weighted verification tools to evaluate univariate and multivariate forecasts for high-impact weather events
authors: Sam Allen, Jonas Bhend, Olivia Martius, Johanna Ziegel
summary: Reviews weighted scoring rules (threshold-weighted CRPS) and weighted PIT histograms for evaluating forecasts of high-impact events.
key_findings: Weighting emphasises extreme outcomes while staying proper. Weighted PIT checks calibration conditional on high outcomes.
coster_takeaway: Evaluate forecasts with twCRPS above 80% fill so model choice is driven by the near-saturation regime that triggers alerts.

title: A comparison of simple heuristics for multi-product dynamic demand lot-sizing with limited warehouse capacity
authors: Stefan Minner
summary: Compares three heuristics for multi-product lot sizing under warehouse space limits against a MIP benchmark.
key_findings: Savings-based heuristic best, especially for large tightly constrained problems.
coster_takeaway: Candidate for later plan adjustment under AW capacity.

title: A Data-Driven Model of an Emergency Department
authors: Ward Whitt; Xiaopei Zhang
summary: Aggregate MT_t/GI_t/inf model of the Rambam hospital ED with weekly-periodic arrivals, time-varying admission probability and LOS.
key_findings: Time-invariant LOS misses departure surge before midnight; LOS by hour of week matches occupancy.
coster_takeaway: Condition dwell distributions on entry weekday and month-end.

title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting (TimesFM)
authors: Das, Kong, Sen, Zhou
summary: Introduces TimesFM, a patched decoder-only model pretrained on a large time-series corpus for zero-shot forecasting.
key_findings: Zero-shot accuracy close to supervised models on public benchmarks (per paper).
coster_takeaway: Background for the TimesFM 2.5/3.0 choice. 2.5 adds XReg covariates (linear covariate model plus TimesFM residual).
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2310.10688 and PMLR v235 (das24c) confirm authors, ICML 2024 and zero-shot accuracy close to supervised models.

title: A Dwell Time-based Container Positioning Decision Support System at a Port Terminal
authors: Myriam Gaete G.; Marcela C. Gonzalez-Araya; Rosa G. Gonzalez-Ramirez; Cesar Astudillo H.
summary: Dwell-time classes predicted by classifiers and evaluated in ExtendSim for yard segregation at Arica.
key_findings: Low accuracy (~7%) but rehandles reduced ~17%.
coster_takeaway: Expect weak individual predictability for externally driven exits; rely on plans where possible.

title: A hybrid analytical model for an entire hospital resource optimisation
authors: Muhammed Ordu; Eren Demir; Soheil Davari
summary: Forecasting of demand feeds a whole-hospital DES whose outputs feed a multi-period MILP for beds, physicians and nurses.
key_findings: Monthly resource needs over a year; sensitivity analysis.
coster_takeaway: Template for chaining forecast -> simulation -> optimisation for later what-if/scheduling.

title: A stochastic analysis of the dynamic space utilization in warehouses
authors: Jin Xu; Yu Chen
summary: Continuous-time Markov chain framework for volume space utilisation in block-stacking warehouses with heterogeneous, stochastic demand and replenishment (lost-sale and backorder models).
key_findings: Closed-form expressions for honeycombing, aisle and top-of-lane space waste; optimal lane depth identified; stochastic model estimates utilisation more accurately than deterministic methods in case studies.
coster_takeaway: Get the full text through the UniTrento library. It may give an analytic model of space utilisation to compare with the flow-balance simulator.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Exa-fetched ScienceDirect page and DOI record show authors Jin Xu and Yu Chen, DOI 10.1016/j.apm.2024.115782 (online Oct 2024, Feb 2025 issue); it is a CTMC model of space waste in block-stacking warehouses.

title: A tabu search algorithm for the relocation problem in a warehousing system
authors: Lu Chen; Andre Langevin; Diane Riopel
summary: Dynamic storage allowing relocations before peak periods so S/R machines can handle peak demand.
key_findings: Selects items and destinations to minimise relocation time while respecting machine availability per period.
coster_takeaway: Analog of pre-peak defrag: schedule relocations ahead of forecast saturation (e.g., before month-end build-up).
check_note: Independent check: corrected. ScienceDirect page shows IJPE 129(1):147-156 (2011), DOI 10.1016/j.ijpe.2010.09.012; content (relocations before peak periods in dynamic storage) matches.

title: An empirical study on yard inventory change according to containers' dwell times
authors: Chang-gon Kim; Myoung-Kil Youn
summary: Analyses weekly yard-inventory changes at container terminals with fixed-day services.
key_findings: Dwell time is a key driver; longer dwell grows inventory even with steady flows; capacity calculations must include weekly schedules and dwell.
coster_takeaway: Weekly shipping rhythm x dwell drives AW occupancy; model both.

title: Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems: A Review on Travel Time Models and Control Policies
authors: M. R. Vasili; Sai Hong Tang; Mehdi Vasili
venue: Chapter 8 in Warehousing in the Global Supply Chain (R. Manzini, ed.), Springer
summary: AS/RS review including WIP storage in factories, equally/unequally sized or modular cells, buffer capacity at I/O, and load shuffling during crane idleness.
key_findings: Design must handle current and future demand while avoiding overcapacity and bottlenecks.
coster_takeaway: Compact reference linking WIP-buffer role, unequal cells and shuffling, the three Coster features.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. PDF is Chapter 8 of 'Warehousing in the Global Supply Chain' (R. Manzini ed., Springer, 2012); it covers WIP storage, equal/unequal/modular cells, I/O buffer capacity and idle-time load shuffling.

title: Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection
authors: Ryan Prescott Adams, David J. C. MacKay
summary: Exact online inference of the run length since the last changepoint by message passing.
key_findings: A modular algorithm, demonstrated on three real datasets.
coster_takeaway: Monitor live residuals and trigger retraining or an ACI reset when the run-length posterior collapses.

title: Betriebspunktuntersuchung des Lagerfüllgrads eines doppeltiefen automatischen Hochregallagers
authors: Timo Lehmann, Paul Knötgen (KIT)
summary: Analytical model for the optimal operating fill level of a double-deep AS/RS, trading space use against relocation-driven cycle-time increases.
key_findings: A variance-minimising storage strategy shortens double-command cycles compared with random storage. Gives a utility-based optimum fill level.
coster_takeaway: Use it to justify the 80% and 90% alert thresholds as operating-point limits rather than arbitrary numbers. Not a forecasting model.

title: Building cyclic master surgery schedules with leveled resulting bed occupancy
authors: Jeroen Belien; Erik Demeulemeester
summary: MIP heuristics and a metaheuristic to build surgery schedules that minimise expected total bed shortage, with stochastic patients per block and LOS.
key_findings: Bed-levelling schedules computed from block assignments.
coster_takeaway: Model for later 'level the AW' scheduling what-if.

title: Can I Park in the City Center? Predicting Car Park Occupancy Rates in Smart Cities
authors: Daniel H. Stolfi, Enrique Alba, Xin Yao
summary: Predicts car-park occupancy rates for Birmingham, Glasgow, Norfolk and Nottingham with polynomial fitting, Fourier series, K-means and time-series methods, validated on unseen data.
key_findings: Built a web service with occupancy forecasts up to one week ahead. The abstract reports no accuracy numbers.
coster_takeaway: Simple seasonal/Fourier baselines are a sensible rung between persistence and ML for 1-7 day occupancy.

title: Can we accurately forecast non-elective bed occupancy and admissions in the NHS? A time-series MSARIMA analysis of longitudinal data from an NHS Trust
authors: Emily Eyles, Maria Theresa Redaniel, Tim Jones, Marion Prat, Tim Keen
summary: MSARIMA forecasts of non-elective admissions and bed occupancy at an NHS trust with calendar and weather regressors.
key_findings: Day of week, holidays and weather improved accuracy. Occupancy was more volatile and harder to forecast than admissions (strict-threshold hit rate 40% vs 60%).
coster_takeaway: Expect the occupancy target to be harder than its flows. Forecast inflows and outflows separately and integrate them (flow balance), with calendar covariates.

title: ChronosX: Adapting Pretrained Time Series Models with Exogenous Variables
authors: Pineda Arango, Mercado, Kapoor, Ansari, Stella, Shen, Senetaire, Turkmen, Shchur, Maddix, Bohlke-Schneider, Wang, Rangapuram
summary: Modular adapters inject past and future covariates into pretrained univariate models without changing the backbone. Introduces 32 synthetic covariate datasets.
key_findings: Outperforms baselines on synthetic and real data. Shows covariates (e.g. promotions) substantially improve forecasts.
coster_takeaway: Supports the hypothesis that the plans (known-future covariates) are Coster's main source of skill. Use Chronos-2 native covariates rather than adapters.

title: Data of dwelling time process at container terminal: Multi-perspective based dataset
authors: Hanung Nindito Prasetyo, Riyanarto Sarno, Dedy Rahman Wijaya, Raden Budiraharjo, Indra Waspada, Kelly Rossa Sungkono
summary: Event log of import-container dwell time (ship discharge to gate-out) from a terminal information system, with worker, waiting-time and cost attributes.
key_findings: Covers 3 months of dwell activity extracted over 6 months. Intended for process discovery, conformance and anomaly detection.
coster_takeaway: Use it as a stay-length/yard-occupancy analogue to test the simulator's sojourn module.

title: Data Quality Problems in Discrete Event Simulation of Manufacturing Operations
authors: Jon Bokrantz, Anders Skoogh, Dan Lämkull, A. Hanna, Terrence Perera
summary: Multiple-case study in automotive firms on data quality problems in DES and the processes that produce the data.
key_findings: Main problems are limited data accessibility, missing data on minor stoppages, and data sources not designed for simulation.
coster_takeaway: Expect the WLog movement log and the MES to be 'not designed for analysis'. Ask for field definitions and timestamp semantics, and plan proxies for missing stoppage data.

title: Developing a Forecasting Simulation Model for Efficient Warehouse Operations
authors: AnyLogic / EPIC InnoLabs
summary: AnyLogic agent-based + DES forecasting model for a Western Digital/DSV warehouse using Excel inputs (inventory state, inbound, outbound, product matrix).
key_findings: 3-month horizon planned to 7 months; no quantitative results yet.
coster_takeaway: Confirms Excel snapshot + inbound + outbound + item master is a workable input contract.

title: Dwell Time Estimation of Import Containers as an Ordinal Regression Problem
authors: Laidy De Armas Jacomino; Miguel Angel Medina-Perez; Raul Monroy; Danilo Valdes-Ramirez; Carlos Morell-Perez; Rafael Bello
summary: Ordinal regression vs classifiers for container dwell time on two small terminal datasets (1,816 and 2,974 records).
key_findings: Ordinal method lowest MAE in 71% and fewest reshuffles in 67% of 21 experiments.
coster_takeaway: If dwell buckets are used, treat them as ordinal.

title: EANCOM DESADV - Despatch advice message (GS1)
authors: GS1
summary: EDI message from seller to buyer that details the contents of a consignment before it moves, optionally with a hierarchical packing structure and SSCC per logistic unit.
key_findings: Lets the receiver plan reception in advance, and discrepancies are caught on arrival by checking against the message.
coster_takeaway: Ask whether Coster's main suppliers send DESADV/ASN or pre-notification emails. Pallet counts 1-3 days ahead are the best short-horizon inbound covariate.

title: Enhanced Parcel Arrival Forecasting for Logistic Hubs: An Ensemble Deep Learning Approach
authors: Xinyue Pan, Yujia Xu, Benoit Montreuil
summary: Short-term hub workload forecasting that fuses historical arrival patterns with real-time parcel status updates in a deep ensemble.
key_findings: Outperforms traditional and standalone deep models in a city-scale case study.
coster_takeaway: Analogue for using shipment notices (FCA 48 h, DAP 24 h) as real-time status covariates for the outflow side.

title: EPCIS 2.0 and Core Business Vocabulary 2.0 (GS1 standard)
authors: GS1
summary: Event-based traceability standard: ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent, AssociationEvent along what/when/where/why/how dimensions. Business step and disposition come from CBV vocabularies.
key_findings: Events carry both eventTime and recordTime. recordTime is 'the date and time at which this event was recorded by an EPCIS Repository', which gives a bitemporal log.
coster_takeaway: Model the unified movement log as EPCIS-like events (LU id, event time, record time, location = cell or floor slot, bizStep, disposition = QC status). This gives clean replay and leak-free backtests.

title: Evaluation of forecasting techniques for short-term demand of air transportation
authors: Richard Robert Wickham
venue: MIT Flight Transportation Laboratory report R95-7
summary: Compares time series, regression and classical/advanced booking pickup for demand under eight weeks before departure.
key_findings: Pickup models best, advanced pickup best overall; more history often hurt.
coster_takeaway: Short training windows are fine for pickup, fitting Coster's short comparable history.

title: Flexible nurse staffing based on hourly bed census predictions
authors: N. Kortbeek, A. Braaksma, C. A. J. Burger, P. J. M. Bakker, R. J. Boucherie
summary: Derives staffing policies from hourly census predictions that depend on arrivals and lengths of stay, in a case at the Academic Medical Center Amsterdam.
key_findings: Hourly census predictions capture within-day fluctuation that daily averages miss. Block planning and unit partitioning interact with staffing.
coster_takeaway: Consider sub-daily occupancy (per shift) for the 48 h alert, since palletiser and shipment waves peak within the day. Partitioning (cell classes) is like partitioned wards.

title: Fluid view of service systems (Service Engineering lecture notes)
authors: Technion Service Engineering course (author not named on slides)
summary: Fluid models replace random arrivals/services by rates; inventory build-up diagrams for predictable rush-hour queues and bottlenecks.
key_findings: Fluid works best for predictable variability; diffusion refinements add noise.
coster_takeaway: Show a cumulative inflow/outflow build-up diagram per class on the dashboard.

title: Foundation Models and Fine-Tuning: Toward a New Generation of Models for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Laglil, Pracca, Devijver, Gaussier
summary: Reviews foundation-model architectures and pretraining, and fine-tunes selected models on specific datasets.
key_findings: Fine-tuning consistently improved over zero-shot on their datasets.
coster_takeaway: Contrasts with the break-even study. Fine-tuning helps with enough data, so revisit Chronos-2 fine-tuning once Coster has 6-12 months post-layout.

title: From a simulation model to a digital twin (part II)
authors: Dirk Becks (Groenewout), with Dirk-Jan Moens and Steven Hamoen (Talumis)
summary: Practitioner view of the data needed to turn a warehouse simulation into a digital twin: layout, process times, live WMS/ERP feeds, historical seasonality.
key_findings: Master data must be accurate and complete. Small timing errors compound (12 s vs 10 s per order over 50,000 orders is about 28 h). Detail should follow the problem being solved.
coster_takeaway: Keep the flow-balance simulator at daily or hourly pallet level. Spend the effort on correct master data (LU type per material, cell compatibility) rather than crane kinematics.

title: From Annual Throughput to Vessel Schedules: A Stochastic Generator for Transshipment Hub Simulation
authors: Qiaohong Li; Haobin Li; Tianhao Chen; Ek Peng Chew
summary: Schedule generator (two-level Gamma model + GreedyDwellFit) for hub simulation instead of Poisson arrivals.
key_findings: Poisson inputs misjudge yard occupancy; generator within 1% on throughput and call frequencies.
coster_takeaway: Generate Monte Carlo inflows from the plan plus structured noise, not Poisson.

title: Generative AI and Machine Learning Collaboration for Container Dwell Time Prediction via Data Standardization
authors: Minseop Kim; Takhyeong Kim; Taekhyun Park; Hanbyeol Park; Hyerim Bae
summary: Generative AI standardises unstructured cargo/owner data; EDI status updates trigger re-prediction of dwell time.
key_findings: MAE improved 13.88%; relocations reduced up to 14.68%.
coster_takeaway: Event-triggered re-prediction of pallet exits when notices/status change.

title: GIFT-Eval: A Benchmark For General Time Series Forecasting Model Evaluation
authors: Aksu, Woo, Liu, Liu, Liu, Savarese, Xiong, Sahoo
summary: 23 datasets, over 144,000 series and 177M points across 7 domains and 10 frequencies, with a non-leaking pretraining corpus. Compares 17 statistical, deep and foundation baselines.
key_findings: Standard leaderboard for zero-shot foundation models. Mainly univariate and multivariate, without covariates.
coster_takeaway: Treat GIFT-Eval ranks as a univariate signal only. Covariate skill must be judged on fev-bench or Coster's own backtest.

title: Hospitalization forecast to inform COVID-19 pandemic planning and resource allocation using mathematical models
authors: Philip Erick Wikman-Jorgensen; Angel Ruiz; Vicente Giner-Galvan; et al.
summary: Stochastic Markov admissions generator feeding an R discrete-event simulation of patient pathways for week-ahead bed occupancy.
key_findings: Median absolute difference about 20 beds/day (~5% of beds) and 4 ICU beds/day (~25% of ICU beds); external validation similar.
coster_takeaway: Generator + DES chain works; errors are proportionally larger for small units (like Coster's 144-192-cell classes).

title: In-Context Fine-Tuning for Time-Series Foundation Models
authors: Abhimanyu Das; Matthew Faw; Rajat Sen; Yichen Zhou
summary: Prompts TimesFM with example series from related series at inference time, so the model adapts few-shot without gradient updates.
key_findings: Google reports few-shot gains over zero-shot (blog 'Time series foundation models can be few-shot learners').
coster_takeaway: Supplying related series (other classes, inflow series) in context is a cheap alternative to fine-tuning on Coster's short history. Chronos-2 group attention offers the same idea.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. arXiv 2410.24087 lists authors Abhimanyu Das, Matthew Faw, Rajat Sen, Yichen Zhou; Google blog confirms ICML 2025 and a 6.8% gain of TimesFM-ICF over base TimesFM.

title: Input data management in simulation - Industrial practices and future trends
authors: Anders Skoogh, Terrence Perera, Björn Johansson
summary: Survey of industrial practice in collecting and preparing input data for discrete-event simulation of production flows.
key_findings: Input data management is the most time-consuming part of simulation maintenance. About 80% of users still rely on highly manual data procedures.
coster_takeaway: Budget most of the project effort for data plumbing. Automate the Excel-to-pandas pipeline with pandera schemas from day one instead of manual cleaning.

title: Integer programming for building robust surgery schedules
authors: Jeroen Belien; Erik Demeulemeester
summary: Daily bed occupancy is the convolution of block contributions with binomial discharge counts; normal approximation; surrogate objectives for expected shortage.
key_findings: Mean and variance of occupancy are linear in decisions, enabling MIP formulations.
coster_takeaway: Shows how to compute occupancy mean/variance per day from a plan analytically.

title: Introducing Artificial Intelligence to Increase Efficiency in Warehouse Logistics: A Case Study
authors: Enej Marinič, Igor Perko
summary: Combines ML forecasts of daily delivery volumes and order quantities with discrete-event simulation of a distribution warehouse.
key_findings: The predictions gave a stable basis for short-term planning. Simulation identified order picking as the bottleneck.
coster_takeaway: Supports Coster's hybrid design (forecast the flows, push them through a simulator). It does not forecast occupancy itself.

title: ISA-95 Common Object Model (OPC UA companion specification OPC 10030), section 4.2.4 Modelling Approach of ISA-95
authors: OPC Foundation / ISA
venue: OPC Foundation reference (based on ANSI/ISA-95 = IEC 62264)
summary: Describes the ISA-95 property-based object model for personnel, equipment, physical assets and material (material class, definition, lot, sublot).
key_findings: A material lot is a uniquely identified instance (shipment or order) that can be assembled from other lots and sublots. Equipment can be nested and carries class properties.
coster_takeaway: Use ISA-95 terms for the data dictionary: material definition = SAP material, material lot/sublot = pallet/pallbox (LU), equipment = cell class and cell. This keeps the SAP-WLog-MES joins unambiguous.

title: Layouts of Unit-Load Warehouses with Multiple Slot Heights
authors: Luis F. Cardona; Kevin R. Gue
summary: Arranges multi-height slots into rack-bays and layouts; simulation and greedy procedure based on duration-of-stay policy.
key_findings: Expected 25-35% space savings and 15-25% lower operating cost with multiple slot heights.
coster_takeaway: Confirms value of duration-of-stay as a simulation driver for multi-height racks.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. INFORMS page: Transportation Science 54(5):1332-1350 (2020); abstract gives 25-35% space savings and 15-25% operating-cost savings with a duration-of-stay simulation/greedy procedure.

title: Machine Learning-Based Predictive Inventory for a Vending Machine Warehouse
authors: Mehmood, Broderick, Davies, Bashir, Rabie
summary: Compares XGBoost, ARIMA/ARIMAX, Prophet and SVR for inventory prediction in a warehouse serving about 1,500 vending machines, with and without exogenous calendar features.
key_findings: MAE: XGBoost 22, ARIMAX 27, Prophet 37, SVR 38. External variables (weekday, holiday flags) significantly improved results.
coster_takeaway: Small-scale evidence that GBMs with calendar and exogenous features beat ARIMAX and Prophet for warehouse stock series.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. MMU e-space record confirms IEEE IoT Magazine 7(6):94-100 (2024), ~1,500 vending machines, and MAE XGBoost 22, ARIMAX 27, Prophet 37, SVR 38 with external variables.

title: Multi-item Simultaneous Lot Sizing and Storage Allocation with Production and Warehouse Capacities
authors: Cagatay Iris
summary: Capacitated lot sizing combined with storage allocation; warehouse limit follows from the allocation policy; two-stage metaheuristic.
key_findings: Storage allocation policy significantly affects outcomes.
coster_takeaway: Capacity per cell class depends on the allocation policy, so model the policy, not just total cells.

title: NeuralForecast exogenous-variable capability overview
authors: Nixtla
summary: Table of future (F), historical (H) and static (S) exogenous support for about 35 neural forecasting models.
key_findings: TFT, TiDE, NHITS, NBEATSx, TSMixerx, DeepAR: F/H/S. PatchTST, NBEATS, TSMixer: none. iTransformer: F only. TimeXer: H and S only.
coster_takeaway: If deep models are revisited later, start with TiDE or TFT, which use known-future plans natively.

title: New lot-sizing formulations for less nervous production schedules
authors: Osman Kazan, Rakesh Nagi, Christopher M. Rump
summary: Defines schedule nervousness (changes between successive rolling-horizon plans) and adds a nervousness cost to lot sizing.
key_findings: Changes include added or cancelled setups and volume changes. Cited evidence shows that freezing the schedule improves stability.
coster_takeaway: Measure Coster's plan nervousness by department from the week of plan versions (share of orders moved or resized per day) and make the slip distribution depend on the frozen flag and the horizon.

title: NGBoost: Natural Gradient Boosting for Probabilistic Prediction
authors: Duan, Avati, Ding, Thai, Basu, Ng, Schuler
summary: Boosts the parameters of a conditional distribution using natural gradients.
key_findings: Matches or exceeds existing probabilistic regression methods. Works with any base learner and scoring rule.
coster_takeaway: An option to get a full distribution, and closed-form P(fill >= 90%), from tabular plan features.

title: On Storage Assignment Policies for Unit-Load Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems
authors: Jean-Philippe Gagliardi; Jacques Renaud; Angel Ruiz
summary: Simulation of an industrial partner's unit-load AS/RS comparing random, class-based and full turnover-based policies.
key_findings: With real constraints, a single-class policy beat full turnover-based storage by up to 19% crane time; results depend on locations per product.
coster_takeaway: Theory-based policies can fail on real AS/RS; calibrate Coster's simulator to observed WLog choices before testing policy what-ifs.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. CIRRELT-2010-25 by Gagliardi, Renaud and Ruiz simulates a Quebec food manufacturer's AS/RS; conclusion states single-class gives up to 19% less crane travel time than FTB and results depend on locations per product.

title: On the Suboptimality of Full Turnover-Based Storage
authors: Yugang Yu; Rene B.M. de Koster
summary: Adapts Hausman et al.'s travel model to dedicated full-turnover storage that must hold maximum inventory.
key_findings: Dedicated storage needs space for maximum inventory; 2-3 class storage normally beats full turnover-based storage.
coster_takeaway: Dedicated or capped allocations (like Coster's weekly cap per material) must be sized to peak, not average, inventory.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. ERIM ERS-2009-051-LIS PDF confirms adapting Hausman et al. to dedicated storage holding maximum inventory and that 2-3 class storage normally outperforms full turnover-based storage.

title: Online Simulation in Semiconductor Manufacturing
authors: Daniel Noack
venue: Doctoral dissertation, Universitaet der Bundeswehr Muenchen
summary: Online simulation for short-term forecasting in a high-mix fab: automatic model generation, data cleaning, initialisation effects, applications catalogue.
key_findings: Initial state dominates short-horizon forecast quality; fab-driven synchronised prototype.
coster_takeaway: Invest in data model and cleaning before model detail.

title: Optimal Storage Assignment in Automatic Warehousing Systems
authors: Warren H. Hausman; Leroy B. Schwarz; Stephen C. Graves
summary: Compares random (similar to closest-open-location), full turnover-based and class-based assignment in stacker-crane systems.
key_findings: Turnover-based rules cut crane travel; trade-off between throughput and storage capacity in design.
coster_takeaway: Foundational reference for policy names; note the shared-storage assumption (space ~ average inventory) when estimating required cells.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. INFORMS abstract (Management Science 22(6), DOI 10.1287/mnsc.22.6.629) compares random (similar to closest-open-location), full turnover and class-based rules and the throughput vs storage capacity trade-off.

title: Optimizing the Rearrangement Process in a Dedicated Warehouse
authors: Hector J. Carlo; German E. Giraldo
summary: Rearrange-While-Working policy relocates items as they are retrieved and re-stored, combined with idle-time shuffling.
key_findings: Heuristics (closest-item, GA) perform well; reviews restoring/shuffling policies for AS/RS using idle times.
coster_takeaway: Coster's partial pallbox returns are a natural RWW opportunity: re-store returning partial loads into smaller classes instead of separate defrag missions.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. Georgia Southern PDF (IMHRC 2010, Progress in Material Handling Research) proposes Rearrange-While-Working combined with idle-time shuffling; closest-item and GA heuristics recommended.

title: Order picking dataset from a warehouse of a footwear manufacturing company
authors: Rodrigo Furlan de Assis, William de Paula Ferreira, Mustapha Ouhimmou
summary: Describes real WMS SQL extracts (locations, positions, picking waves, routes, timestamps) plus CAD layouts and scripts from a footwear manufacturer's warehouse.
key_findings: Data is anonymised and randomised but keeps realistic patterns. It supports comparing random, class-based, dedicated and hybrid storage strategies.
coster_takeaway: Borrow its data-model structure (location master + movements) when specifying the WLog extract.

title: Prediction of parking space availability in real time
authors: Felix Caicedo; Carola Blazquez; Pablo Miranda
summary: Allocates simulated reservation requests with a discrete-choice model, estimates departures and forecasts availability.
key_findings: Small average errors; accuracy improves as arrivals/departures are recorded.
coster_takeaway: Choice-based allocation across facilities parallels the cell-class cascade.

title: Research on warehouse operation: A comprehensive review
authors: Jinxiang Gu; Marc Goetschalckx; Leon F. McGinnis
summary: Framework of warehouse operation planning problems: receiving, storage (how much, when, where), order picking, shipping.
key_findings: Storage decisions split into lot sizing, staggering and location assignment; warehouses buffer production batching and seasonality.
coster_takeaway: Frames Coster's AW as a buffer of production batching; inventory level and location assignment must be modelled jointly.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. ScienceDirect page (EJOR 177(1):1-21, 2007) confirms the framework, warehouses buffering production batching/seasonality, and storage decisions leading to lot sizing, staggering and location assignment.

title: Robotized and Automated Warehouse Systems: Review and Recent Developments
authors: Kaveh Azadeh; Rene B.M. de Koster; Debjit Roy
summary: Reviews shuttle-based, compact and robotic mobile systems; literature grouped into analysis, design and operations control.
key_findings: Integration of subsystems (vehicles + storage) is under-studied; new models needed for networked dynamic operation.
coster_takeaway: Background for LGV+AS/RS interaction; supports treating LGV capacity as a separate constraint from cell capacity.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. INFORMS page (Transportation Science, published June 2019) abstract confirms review of shuttle-based, compact and RMFS systems in analysis/design/control groups and need for models for integration of subsystems.

title: Sequential Predictive Conformal Inference for Time Series (SPCI)
authors: Chen Xu, Yao Xie
summary: Quantile regression on past residuals exploits their autocorrelation to build intervals.
key_findings: Asymptotically valid conditional coverage. Significantly narrower intervals than existing methods.
coster_takeaway: Consider once 6-12 months of residuals exist. Too data-hungry now.

title: State of the Art and Future Directions of Digital Twins for Production Logistics: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Alexander Kaiblinger, Manuel Woschank
summary: Systematic review of digital twins in production logistics, covering data integration with ERP/MES/PLM, synchronisation and implementation maturity.
key_findings: A bidirectional link to enterprise systems is necessary, and the MES is often the central data hub. No standard data model or architecture exists, and few full industrial twins are implemented.
coster_takeaway: Treat the SQL Server staging DB that links SAP, WLog, MES and LGV as the twin's data hub. Ask for read access there instead of many Excel exports.

title: Supply chain data analytics for predicting supplier disruptions: a case study in complex asset manufacturing
authors: Alexandra Brintrup, Johnson Pak, David Ratiney, Tim Pearce, Pascal Wichmann, Philip Woodall, Duncan McFarlane
summary: Machine learning on historical OEM order data to predict first-tier supplier late deliveries.
key_findings: Engineered 'agility' features gave the best model, predicting late orders with about 80% accuracy. Domain knowledge was key for feature engineering.
coster_takeaway: Supplier-level lateness features (history of slips, order size, frequency) are a cheap rung-3 residual feature for inbound pallets.

title: SupplyGraph: A Benchmark Dataset for Supply Chain Planning using Graph Neural Networks
authors: Azmine Toushik Wasi, MD Shafikul Islam, Adipto Raihan Akib
summary: Releases a real FMCG supply-chain graph (41 products, plant and storage-location edges) with temporal production, sales-order, delivery and factory-issue features for Jan-Aug 2023.
key_findings: Data was manually reviewed for anomalies and zeros. The benchmark supports homogeneous and heterogeneous graph tasks for demand and production planning.
coster_takeaway: Use it as a short real production-in/issues-out panel to test the flow-balance rung and lead-lag between sales orders and outflows.

title: The M5 uncertainty competition: Results, findings and conclusions
authors: Makridakis, Spiliotis, Assimakopoulos, Chen, Gaba, Tsetlin, Winkler
topics: benchmark; covariates_known_future; demand_forecasting; hierarchical_forecasting; probabilistic_forecasting; time_series_ml
summary: Companion competition asking for 9 quantiles (0.005 to 0.995) of 42,840 hierarchical series.
key_findings: Established quantile (pinball-loss) evaluation at scale. Details of the winning methods are in the full paper.
