coster_takeaway: Evaluate Coster's bands with pinball loss or CRPS at several quantiles, not only coverage.

title: Time-varying queues
authors: Ward Whitt
summary: Review of time-varying queues, focused on many-server systems such as call centres and emergency departments, with heavy-traffic limits.
key_findings: Infinite-server and offered-load approximations underpin time-varying capacity analysis.
coster_takeaway: Reference for the M_t/G/inf and offered-load approximations used in rung 2 extensions.

title: TiRex: Zero-Shot Forecasting Across Long and Short Horizons with Enhanced In-Context Learning
authors: Auer, Podest, Klotz, Böck, Klambauer, Hochreiter
summary: 35M-parameter xLSTM (sLSTM) forecaster with Contiguous Patch Masking that outputs 9 quantiles.
key_findings: GIFT-Eval zero-shot CRPS 0.411 vs 0.459 for the next best. Strong at both short and long horizons. Univariate only; covariates are future work.
coster_takeaway: A good small univariate foundation-model reference to measure how much the covariates add.

title: Warehouse & Distribution Science (Release 0.94)
authors: John J. Bartholdi III, Steven T. Hackman
venue: Georgia Tech Supply Chain and Logistics Institute (open textbook)
summary: Open textbook on warehouse design and operations, including Little's law for storage space and dedicated vs shared storage utilisation.
key_findings: Inventory = arrival rate x time in storage (L = lambda W) at any aggregation level. Shared storage over k locations averages about k/(k+1) utilisation, dedicated storage about 50%.
coster_takeaway: Sanity-check each class: average occupied cells should be close to pallets in per day x mean dwell days. Large gaps point to missing flows (floor buffer, empties, defrag).

title: Warehouse Digital Twin: Simulation Modeling and Analysis Techniques
authors: Michael E. Kuhl; Rukshar Bhisti; Sriparvathi Shaji Bhattathiri; Maojia P. Li
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Framework for a continuously updated warehouse twin (physical system, data/control, simulation, experimentation) that can simulate the near future.
key_findings: Illustrative applications; interoperability and data collection are open challenges.
coster_takeaway: Later target architecture; start with a lightweight data-driven model.

title: Warehouse reshuffling: Insights and optimization
authors: Jennifer A. Pazour; Hector J. Carlo
summary: Optimises reshuffling of unit loads to restore a better storage assignment.
key_findings: Mathematical programming formulation and complexity of the general reshuffling problem; heuristics that relax cycle handling and allow double-handling beat a benchmark heuristic; managerial insights on reshuffling policies in various environments.
coster_takeaway: Reference for modelling defrag as a planned set of relocation moves with limited idle time.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. RePEc/Crossref: TR-E 73:207-226 (2015); abstract gives a general reshuffling formulation, complexity, heuristics and double-handling proof, not a statement of when reshuffling pays off.

title: Why Initial Conditions Are Important
authors: Bruce Gunn; Saeid Nahavandi
venue: Proceedings of the 2002 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Shows a batch-manufacturing simulation cannot be credible without initial WIP; traced outstanding orders into buffers.
key_findings: Zero-WIP model never reached observed WIP; lead times differed 2-3 days.
coster_takeaway: Initial stock per class must come from the snapshot, never from an empty start.

title: A performance estimation model for AS/RS by M/G/1 queuing system
authors: Sun Hur; Young Hae Lee; Si Yeong Lim; Moon Hwan Lee
summary: Queueing model of AS/RS performance.
key_findings: Analytical estimation of crane waiting/throughput.
coster_takeaway: Optional: crane queueing if throughput (not cells) limits Coster in peaks.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. ScienceDirect abstract (C&IE 46(2):233-241, 2004) describes an M/G/1 model with two queues giving the steady-state distribution of waiting storage/retrieval commands, validated against simulation.

title: A review of design and control of automated guided vehicle systems
authors: Tuan Le-Anh; Rene B.M. de Koster
summary: Covers guide-path design, fleet sizing, scheduling, idle-vehicle positioning, battery management, routing, conflicts.
key_findings: Proposes a new dispatching-rule classification and a decision framework for design and control of AGV systems; also covers often-neglected idle-vehicle positioning and battery management.
coster_takeaway: Reference if LGV fleet (5 vehicles) becomes a modelled bottleneck.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. The URL is the 2004 ERIM report version; the EJOR 171(1):1-23 (2006) version has DOI 10.1016/j.ejor.2005.01.036; abstracts cover the listed topics and a decision framework but say nothing about online dispatching being common.

title: A survey on single crane scheduling in automated storage/retrieval systems
authors: Nils Boysen; Konrad Stephan
summary: Classification scheme and exact algorithms/complexity results for single-crane scheduling problems.
key_findings: Provides notation for crane request sequencing; mostly throughput-oriented.
coster_takeaway: Low direct relevance; useful if crane throughput becomes a binding constraint in what-if scenarios.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. RePEc page confirms EJOR 254(3):691-704 (2016), DOI and a classification scheme with exact algorithms and complexity results for single-crane scheduling.

title: Adaptive Online Optimization of Business Processes
authors: Maksym Avramenko
summary: Reconstructs current process state from partial event logs to start short-term simulation without warm-up (ProcState in Prosimos).
key_findings: Matched real-log workload exactly; timing comparable except BPIC17.
coster_takeaway: Fallback for reconstructing state from the movement log if snapshots are missing.

title: An Approach for Increasing the Level of Accuracy in Supply Chain Simulation by Using Patterns on Input Data
authors: Markus Rabe, Anne Antonia Scheidler
venue: Proceedings of the 2014 Winter Simulation Conference
summary: Adds knowledge discovery (rule mining) to input data preparation for supply chain simulation, tested on a motorcycle manufacturer's database.
key_findings: Raw data contained outliers, constant redundant attributes (107 reduced to 67) and impossible timestamps (year 2201). Joins exploded to about 201 M rows.
coster_takeaway: Run automatic sanity checks on exports: impossible timestamps, constant columns, orphan keys. Mine simple rules (e.g., which LU types go to which classes) from the movement log.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
authors: Ansari et al.
summary: Tokenises scaled values and trains T5 language models on time series for zero-shot probabilistic forecasting.
key_findings: Strong zero-shot accuracy on many datasets. Univariate, no covariates.
coster_takeaway: Superseded by Chronos-2 for Coster.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2403.07815 PDF header confirms TMLR (10/2024); T5 models on scaled/quantized tokens, strong zero-shot on 42-dataset benchmark.

title: Ciw: An open source discrete event simulation library
authors: Geraint I. Palmer; Vincent A. Knight; Paul R. Harper; Asyl L. Hawa
summary: Python DES library for open queueing networks emphasising reproducibility, with performance comparison.
key_findings: Supports blocking, baulking, server schedules, customer classes.
coster_takeaway: Not a good fit for heterogeneous cells; prefer SimPy/plain numpy.

title: Data leakage in backtesting (PredictHQ documentation)
authors: PredictHQ
summary: Vendor guidance on whether revisions to future-event features cause leakage when backtesting demand models without point-in-time snapshots.
key_findings: Only revisions known after the forecast point are leakage. In their study, horizons up to about 6 weeks showed no measurable accuracy shift because most events are entered months ahead.
coster_takeaway: The opposite holds for Coster: plans change inside the 14-day horizon (~10% unrealised in 10 days). Point-in-time plan snapshots are therefore necessary.

title: Data Set: Spatiotemporal Bikeshare System Status
authors: Not stated on landing page
summary: Cleaned, nearly minute-level station status (bikes and open docks) for Capital Bikeshare, Apr 2019 - Sep 2022, linkable to trip records.
key_findings: Includes dock-less bikes introduced during the period. Raw errors were corrected.
coster_takeaway: Long, multi-unit capacity/occupancy history with flows. Useful for stress-testing the 'unit full' alert logic.

title: Design, simulation and performance of a highly-dynamic, hybrid pallet storage and retrieval system
authors: Giulia Siciliano; T. Lienert; Johannes Fottner
summary: Discrete-event simulation of a stacker-crane AS/RS combined with a shuttle base used as intermediate buffer.
key_findings: Intermediate buffering absorbs short-term fluctuations and raises throughput.
coster_takeaway: Supports DES for buffer interplay (AW vs floor buffer).
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. MAS 2020 (I3M) abstract confirms a stacker-crane AS/RS combined with an AVS/RS shuttle base whose intermediate buffering raises throughput and absorbs short-term fluctuations, modelled by DES.

title: Digital twin-based warehouse management system: a theoretical toolbox for future research and applications
authors: Pratik Maheshwari, Sachin Kamble, Satish Kumar, Amine Belhadi, Shivam Gupta
venue: The International Journal of Logistics Management 35(4), 1073-1106
summary: Systematic literature analysis of digital twins for warehouse management: problems addressed, interoperability, control towers and a research framework.
key_findings: Interoperability, integrability and cross-platform interfaces are the central challenges. Ontologies and knowledge graphs are proposed for DT-based WMS.
coster_takeaway: Use it as background for the twin roadmap. Its practical lesson for Coster is to agree a shared identifier and data dictionary across SAP, WLog, MES and LGV first.

title: Exact Aggregation for Inventory Distribution in an Automatic Warehousing System
authors: Hideaki Yamashita; Hiroshi Ohtani; Shigemichi Suzuki
venue: Journal of the Operations Research Society of Japan 41(4)
summary: Markov chain of slot full/empty states in an AS/RS with Poisson retrievals and batch replenishment; exact aggregation reduces 2^m states.
key_findings: Marginal slot-full probabilities computable in O(m^4) overall.
coster_takeaway: Markov-chain treatment of cell states is tractable only with aggregation; use class-level counts.

title: Forecasting Storage Demand in Multi-Tenant Cloud ERP Systems
authors: Ella Djärv, Sebastian Karlsson
summary: Forecasts data-storage capacity: gradient boosting for new tenants with no history, and statistical models and Prophet for the platform-level daily series.
key_findings: Platform growth is trend-driven, so simple models suffice. The GBM is biased toward overestimation, which the authors consider the safer error.
coster_takeaway: Analogue for capacity forecasting: choose asymmetric (overestimating) loss or high quantiles when the cost of saturation exceeds the cost of a false alarm.

title: HHLA to predict container dwell time with machine learning solutions
authors: Port Technology International (news)
summary: HHLA integrated ML dwell/pick-up predictions into slot allocation at CTA and CTB.
key_findings: Significant positive effect reported, no figures.
coster_takeaway: Industrial precedent for dwell prediction feeding allocation.

title: HierarchicalForecast (Nixtla) library
authors: Olivares et al.
summary: Python implementation of BottomUp, TopDown, MiddleOut, MinTrace and ERM plus probabilistic reconciliation (Normality, Bootstrap, PERMBU, Conformal).
key_findings: Apache-2.0. Integrates with StatsForecast, MLForecast and NeuralForecast.
coster_takeaway: Use if a total-AW view is needed in the dashboard.

title: Inbound Logistic Volume Estimation (success story)
authors: appliedAI Initiative GmbH
summary: Case where ML forecasts of supplier inbound delivery volumes, using supplier data and public indicators, supported production and warehouse planning.
key_findings: Reported about 20% better warehouse utilisation and up to 25% higher customer satisfaction. Data fields and method are not disclosed.
coster_takeaway: Shows inbound-volume forecasting as a standalone module. For Coster, purchased-goods inbound is the most uncertain flow and deserves its own model.

title: Inventory Record Inaccuracy: An Empirical Analysis
authors: Nicole DeHoratius, Ananth Raman
summary: Empirical study of almost 370,000 inventory records across 37 stores of one retailer, analysing drivers of record inaccuracy.
key_findings: 65% of records were inaccurate. Auditing reduces and environmental complexity increases inaccuracy. Variance is explained mostly at the product-category level.
coster_takeaway: Do not assume the WLog snapshot is ground truth. Quantify ghost or missing LUs by reconciling snapshots against the movement log and plan a periodic audit check.

title: Long-term Forecasting with TiDE: Time-series Dense Encoder
authors: Das, Kong, Leach, Mathur, Sen, Yu
summary: MLP encoder-decoder that conditions on past and future covariates.
key_findings: Fast and competitive with transformers on long-horizon benchmarks (per authors).
coster_takeaway: The first deep model to try once a year of post-layout data exists.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. arXiv/ML Anthology: exact title is 'Long-term Forecasting with TiDE: Time-series Dense Encoder', TMLR 2023, 6 authors; MLP encoder-decoder with covariates, 5-10x faster than best Transformer.

title: Machine Learning for Storage Location Prediction in Industrial High Bay Warehouses
authors: Fabian Berns, T. Ramsdorf, Christian Beecks
summary: Data-driven storage-type classification for an industrial high-bay warehouse using production data from a large Danish retailer.
key_findings: Argues that only transparent models are acceptable in logistics. Relevant expert knowledge is often not digitised.
coster_takeaway: If the cascade rules cannot be documented, learn the empirical class assignment per LU type from the movement log with an interpretable model (decision tree) and confirm it with Coster.

title: MARDH in SAP S/4HANA is different from MARDH in SAP ERP (SAP blog)
authors: SAP Community member
summary: Explains that in S/4HANA the stock-history table MARDH is a compatibility view (NSDM_E_MARDH) computed from MATDOC_EXTRACT, not a physical table.
key_findings: S/4HANA writes a MARDH row for every period (about 25x more rows in one report). Points to SAP Notes 2206980 and 2600024 on the new inventory data model.
coster_takeaway: If historical SAP stock levels per storage location are needed, extract them from MATDOC-based CDS views rather than legacy tables. Expect volume and performance issues.

title: Minimizing the peak load in a shared storage system based on the duration-of-stay of unit loads
authors: Lu Chen; Diane Riopel; Andre Langevin
venue: International Journal of Shipping and Transport Logistics 1(1):20-36 (GERAD G-2008-18)
summary: MIP and two heuristics for DoS-based shared storage minimising peak daily processing load.
key_findings: Peak load is an alternative assignment criterion.
coster_takeaway: Background on DoS-based storage with capacity/peak criteria.

title: Modeling for Non-Exponential Production Systems Using Parts Flow Data: Model Parameter Estimation and Performance Analysis
authors: Yuting Sun, Liang Zhang
summary: Estimates production-line parameters from buffer-level part counts (entries, exits, occupancy per time slot) instead of machine up/down logs, using neural surrogates and PSO.
key_findings: Buffer counts are easier to collect than machine status data, which suffer from 'high complexity and low quality'. Machine efficiencies are identifiable, other parameters are not unique.
coster_takeaway: If MES downtime data are poor, use counts of pallets into and out of the AW per department as the main signal and infer effective production rates from them.

title: Moirai 2.0: When Less Is More for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Liu, Aksu, Liu, Liu, Yan, Pham, Savarese, Xiong, Li
summary: Decoder-only model with quantile loss and multi-token prediction, trained on 36M series. About 30x smaller and 2x faster than Moirai 1.0-Large.
key_findings: Among the top pretrained models on GIFT-Eval. Performance plateaus with size and degrades at long horizons. Univariate only, with no cross-variate forecasting. Weights CC-BY-NC-4.0.
coster_takeaway: Not suitable: it cannot use plans and the license is non-commercial.

title: OCEL (Object-Centric Event Log) 2.0 Specification
authors: Alessandro Berti, István Koren, Jan Niklas Adams, Gyunam Park, Benedikt Knopp, Nina Graves, Majid Rafiei, Lukas Liß, Leah Tacke Genannt Unterberg, Yisong Zhang, Christopher Schwanen, Marco Pegoraro, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
summary: A standard for event logs where events link to multiple typed objects, with qualified object-to-object relations and timestamped object attribute changes.
key_findings: Supports XML, JSON and SQLite. Simulated logistics, procure-to-pay and inventory logs follow it.
coster_takeaway: Consider modelling the joined SAP/WLog/MES/LGV extract as an object-centric log (pallet, order, cell, LGV). It makes movement-log cleaning and replay simpler.

title: Optimal forecast reconciliation for hierarchical and grouped time series through trace minimization
authors: Shanika L. Wickramasuriya, George Athanasopoulos, Rob J. Hyndman
summary: MinT reconciliation: coherent forecasts that minimise total forecast-error variance using the full error covariance.
key_findings: Closed-form and scalable. Performs well in simulations and on tourism data.
coster_takeaway: Optional: reconcile class forecasts with total AW fill. Low gain for a 5-to-1 hierarchy.

title: Outbound Modeling for Inventory Management
authors: Riccardo Savorgnan, Udaya Ghai, Carson Eisenach, Dean Foster
summary: Probabilistic model of per-warehouse outbound drain and shipping cost, conditioned on inventory positions and exogenous demand, used as a differentiable simulator for RL.
key_findings: A learned outbound model replaces slow, non-differentiable fulfilment systems. Validation on counterfactual inventory states is proposed.
coster_takeaway: Supports modelling outflow as a function of current state (what is stored) plus demand, not demand alone. Feed the snapshot composition into the outflow model.

title: PUNDIT: Predicting hospital Usage Numbers via a DIgital Twin
authors: University of Southampton; University Hospital Southampton (NIHR ARC Wessex)
summary: Feasibility project for a simulation digital twin predicting short-term bed occupancy under intervention scenarios.
key_findings: No results on page.
coster_takeaway: Forecast + scenario in one tool is the target end state.

title: Rack cell configuration problem: a mathematical model and effective combined heuristic
authors: Andrzej Ratkiewicz; Konrad Lewczuk
venue: Bulletin of the Polish Academy of Sciences: Technical Sciences 69(1)
summary: Combinatorial model and heuristic for configuring rack cells for heterogeneous unit types (all dimensions, weights, rotations).
key_findings: Cells must fit all unit types with safety gaps; bay dimensions are hard to change, beam heights adjustable.
coster_takeaway: Useful if Coster revisits the cell-class mix (re-beaming) as a capacity lever in what-ifs.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. Bull. Pol. Acad. Sci. Tech. Sci. 69(1) e135836 (2021) abstract and intro confirm the RCCP model/heuristic, cells fitting all unit types with safety gaps, adjustable beam heights and hard-to-change bays.

title: salabim: discrete event simulation and animation in Python
authors: Ruud van der Ham
summary: Python DES and animation library.
key_findings: Components, queues, resources, stores, states, monitors; 2D/3D animation; MIT.
coster_takeaway: Optional for animated what-if demos.

title: SAP S/4HANA EWM important tables (SAP Community blog)
authors: SAP Community member
summary: Lists key EWM tables: /SCWM/AQUA (available stock), /SCWM/QUAN (physical stock attributes), /SCWM/LAGP (bins), /SCWM/ORDIM_O and /SCWM/ORDIM_C (open and confirmed warehouse tasks), /SCWM/HUHDR (HU header).
key_findings: EWM separates bins, quants, HUs and warehouse tasks. Confirmed tasks form the movement log.
coster_takeaway: Coster runs its own WMS (WLog), so these are only a reference for how a clean bin/quant/task model looks. Map WLog tables to the same four concepts.

title: Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC)
authors: GS1 Australia
summary: 18-digit GS1 key that uniquely identifies a logistic unit (pallet, case) for its lifetime, encodable in barcode or RFID and shared through EDI or EPCIS.
key_findings: Structure: AI (00) + extension digit + company prefix + serial reference + check digit. Links unit status to despatch advice and speeds goods receipt.
coster_takeaway: Check whether Coster's pallet labels carry an SSCC or an internal LU number used consistently in SAP, WLog and the LGV DB. That key is needed to join movements, missions and orders.

title: Sorting multibay block stacking storage systems
authors: Jakob Pfrommer; Thomas Boemer; Daniyar Akizhanov; Anne Meyer
summary: Unit-load pre-marshalling in block-stacking storage with AMRs during off-peak times, in anticipation of future demand from production schedules or truck slots.
key_findings: Two-step approach (access direction, then move sequence) with A* and constraint programming.
coster_takeaway: Relevant if Coster's floor buffer is block-stacked: off-peak LGV pre-marshalling ahead of planned retrievals.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. arXiv 2405.04847 confirms authors and content (multibay block stacking, AMR pre-marshalling off-peak, access direction then move sequence, A* and CP); the arXiv page also gives journal DOI 10.1016/j.cor.2025.107359.

title: Sundial: A Family of Highly Capable Time Series Foundation Models
authors: Liu, Qin, Shi, Chen, Yang, Huang, Wang, Long
summary: Generative foundation models trained with a flow-matching TimeFlow loss on TimeBench (1 trillion points).
key_findings: Reports state-of-the-art point and probabilistic results and millisecond inference. No covariates.
coster_takeaway: Low priority: no covariates.

title: Survey of research in the design and control of automated guided vehicle systems
authors: Iris F.A. Vis
summary: Reviews AGV system design and control (flowpaths, vehicle requirements, dispatching, routing) in manufacturing, distribution and terminals.
key_findings: AGV research is entering a new phase with large fleets in distribution, transshipment and transport; these differ from manufacturing in fleet size, utilisation, number of tasks and distances travelled.
coster_takeaway: Background for LGV capacity as a possible constraint in what-ifs (extra truck, peak shipping).
check_note: Independent check: corrected. ScienceDirect/RePEc confirm EJOR 170(3):677-709 (2006) and scope; the claim about vehicle-requirement and dispatching models depending on release/due times was not found, the conclusion stresses large AGV fleets in new application areas.

title: The Analysis of Queues with Time-Varying Rates for Telecommunication Models
authors: William A. Massey
summary: Introduces canonical queueing models with time-varying rates and the tools to analyse them, with telecom applications.
key_findings: Covers lag between peak arrivals and peak load.
coster_takeaway: Background theory only.

title: This Time is Different: An Observability Perspective on Time Series Foundation Models (Toto, BOOM)
authors: Cohen, Khwaja, Doubli, et al.
summary: Toto, a 151M decoder-only model trained heavily on observability telemetry, and BOOM, a benchmark of 2,807 series and 350M observations.
key_findings: State of the art on BOOM. Apache-2.0 weights. No covariate support evaluated.
coster_takeaway: Low priority for Coster: no covariates, and the pretraining domain is far from warehouse stocks.

title: TimeXer: Empowering Transformers for Time Series Forecasting with Exogenous Variables
authors: Wang et al. (Tsinghua THUML)
summary: Patch-level endogenous tokens and variate-level exogenous tokens with cross-attention.
key_findings: Strong results on exogenous-variable benchmarks (per authors). NeuralForecast exposes historical and static exog only.
coster_takeaway: Not for now. Note that it handles exogenous history and not future plans in NeuralForecast.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv and NeurIPS 2024 proceedings PDF confirm TimeXer design; NeuralForecast capability table lists TimeXer with historical and static exogenous only.

title: Toward Reducing Unproductive Container Moves: Predicting Service Requirements and Dwell Times
authors: Elena Villalobos; Adolfo De Unanue T.; Fernanda Sobrino; David Ake; Stephany Cisneros; Jorge Lecona; Alejandra Matadamaz
summary: ML predicts pre-clearance service needs and dwell times from terminal operational data, with text classification and record deduplication.
key_findings: Outperforms rule-based heuristics and random baselines across temporal validation periods.
coster_takeaway: Temporal validation across several periods is the right backtest design.

title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers (Moirai)
authors: Woo, Liu, Kumar, Xiong, Savarese, Sahoo
summary: Moirai: a masked-encoder universal forecaster with any-variate attention and a mixture output distribution, trained on LOTSA.
key_findings: Early foundation model designed for arbitrary numbers of variates and covariates.
coster_takeaway: Historical context only. Moirai 2.0 dropped cross-variate support and the weights are research-only.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. PMLR v235 (pp. 53140-53164) confirms Moirai, ICML 2024, authors and LOTSA training.

title: Using a comprehensive digital twin to reduce high-bay warehouse commissioning time by 30 percent (Ferrero)
authors: Siemens Digital Industries Software
summary: Plant Simulation + PLCSIM Advanced twin for virtual commissioning of Ferrero's Alba high-bay warehouse (8,000 pallet spaces, 4 cranes).
key_findings: Commissioning 13 vs 19 weeks (~30% less); 98% availability in 3 weeks; twin up to 50,000x real time.
coster_takeaway: Equipment twins are for commissioning, not occupancy forecasting.

title: Using Big Data to Enhance the Bosch Production Line Performance: A Kaggle Challenge
authors: Ankita Mangal, Nishant Kumar
summary: Describes the Bosch Kaggle dataset (51 stations, 4 lines, about 1.18M parts, about 6-min timestamps) and an XGBoost failure-prediction pipeline.
key_findings: XGBoost CV AUC 0.718. Adding time-based features raised leaderboard MCC from 0.215 to 0.407. Data shows weekly periodicity and about 7,150 unique flow paths.
coster_takeaway: Even in production data, timing/calendar features carry most of the signal. Prioritise them in the residual model.

title: Warehouse space capacity and delivery time window considerations in dynamic lot-sizing for a simple supply chain
authors: not shown on fetched page
summary: Two-echelon dynamic lot sizing with delivery time windows and limited warehouse space; O(T^3) dynamic program.
key_findings: Polynomial-time optimal replenishment and dispatch plans.
coster_takeaway: Background for capacity-constrained planning.

title: Warehouse stock volumes forecasting (Enfint case study)
authors: Enfint
summary: Forecast of warehouse stock volumes across departments of a large logistics operator (400,000 m2 of warehouses) for transport planning.
key_findings: Tested STL+SARIMA, ARIMA+Fourier, TBATS, Prophet and LSTM. SARIMA was best (median weighted percentage error about 28%), and planning accuracy improved by more than 5%.
coster_takeaway: Univariate warehouse-stock forecasts reach only moderate accuracy. Coster's known plans should beat this, which argues for plan-driven models.

title: Digital Twins: Warehouses of the Future
authors: Faisal Ali Moutaz; Yumeng Chen
summary: Digital twin prototype and ML workforce forecasting for order picking.
key_findings: Feasibility and roadmap; no measured results in abstract.
coster_takeaway: Low relevance.

title: Exploring the representativeness of the M5 competition data
authors: Evangelos Theodorou, Shengjie Wang, Yanfei Kang, Evangelos Spiliotis, Spyros Makridakis, Vassilios Assimakopoulos
summary: Compares M5 series characteristics with other retail datasets to judge how representative M5 is.
key_findings: 73.35% of M5 series are intermittent, a key difference from the comparison datasets.
coster_takeaway: Retail benchmarks differ structurally from occupancy series. Do not over-read M5 results for Coster.

title: Forecasting time series with complex seasonal patterns using exponential smoothing (TBATS)
authors: Alysha M. De Livera, Rob J. Hyndman, Ralph D. Snyder
summary: Innovations state space model with Box-Cox transforms, trigonometric seasonality and ARMA errors.
key_findings: Handles multiple and non-integer seasonalities with analytic intervals.
coster_takeaway: Not needed: Coster has too little history for multi-seasonal models.

title: Identifying the optimum warehouse capacity requirement: A system dynamics approach
authors: Lewlyn L. R. Rodrigues; Farahnaz Golrooy Motlagh; Srinivasa Rao; Sunith Hebbar
summary: System dynamics model of a trading system to find optimum warehouse space for class-A products.
key_findings: Optimum about 825 products (55%); reduced bullwhip near indicated orders.
coster_takeaway: SD is for long-term policy only; not for 1-14 day forecasts.

title: Integrated Versus Sequential Scheduling and Assignment at a Unit Load Cross-Dock
authors: Arpan Rijal; Marco Bijvank; Rene de Koster
venue: MHI Progress in Material Handling Research colloquium 2016
summary: Integer programs for truck scheduling and door assignment at a unit-load cross-dock with temporary storage cost.
key_findings: Assumes unlimited storage space; integrated model up to 6.5% better but slower.
coster_takeaway: Scheduling models often ignore storage capacity; Coster's must not.

title: Lag-Llama: Towards Foundation Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
authors: Rasul, Ashok, Williams, et al.
summary: Decoder-only univariate probabilistic foundation model that uses lagged values as covariates.
key_findings: Good zero-shot generalisation. Fine-tuning on small portions of new data reaches state of the art (per authors).
coster_takeaway: Not relevant: no exogenous plans.

title: Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive
authors: Rakshitha Godahewa, Christoph Bergmeir, Geoffrey I. Webb, Rob J. Hyndman, Pablo Montero-Manso
summary: Curated archive of 25 public time-series datasets with feature analysis and baseline results on ten error metrics.
key_findings: Datasets differ in frequency, length and missingness. Provides standard baselines for comparison.
coster_takeaway: Low priority. Use only for generic baseline sanity checks.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks 2021 page confirms authors, 25 datasets and ten error metrics.

title: Time-MoE: Billion-Scale Time Series Foundation Models with Mixture of Experts
authors: Shi, Wang, Nie, Li, Ye, Wen, Jin
summary: Sparse mixture-of-experts decoder models up to 2.4B params, pretrained on Time-300B.
key_findings: Better than dense models at equal activated compute (per authors).
coster_takeaway: Not relevant: heavy and without covariates.
